matchstick.title: Vertical sticks in simple numerals
matchstick.principle: I, II, III, and L are built only from vertical matchsticks. Adding or removing a single vertical stick changes the numeral by exactly one unit (or creates a valid adjacent numeral).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains only these numerals and you need to adjust a value by one.
matchstick.example: Add a vertical stick to I to get II, or remove one from II to get I.

matchstick.title: Preserve token validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, both the source token (with a stick removed) and the destination token (with a stick added) must still be recognizable as a valid Roman numeral or allowed operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For any stick move, verify that the resulting shapes correspond to permitted symbols.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=' yields '-', which is valid; adding it to '-' yields '=', also valid.

matchstick.title: Use numeric difference to guide moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of each side of the equation; the difference tells how many units need to be added or removed, guiding which numerals or operators to modify.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before deciding which stick to move, evaluate the arithmetic gap between the two sides.
matchstick.example: If LHS = 15 and RHS = 5, you need to reduce LHS by 10 or increase RHS by 10.

matchstick.title: I‑V reordering changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: Moving an I across a V changes the order from IV (4) to VI (6) or vice versa, altering the value by exactly two.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the pattern IV or VI appears and a vertical stick can be relocated across the V.
matchstick.example: Turning IV into VI by moving the I to the right of V adds 2.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from one numeral to another reduces the source’s value by one and raises the destination’s value by one, while keeping both tokens valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust two numerals in opposite directions by one unit each.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical from II to I changes them to I and II.

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X consist solely of diagonal sticks; removing a diagonal leaves an invalid shape, so they should never be used as a source of a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a potential move involves taking a stick from V or X.
matchstick.example: Do not try to turn X into I by removing a diagonal.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity
matchstick.principle: When moving sticks that belong to operators, the resulting symbol must still be one of the allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any move that modifies an operator.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' swaps them, both remain valid operators.

matchstick.title: Final verification of equation
matchstick.principle: After performing a stick move, recompute the values of all numerals and confirm that the arithmetic equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of the reasoning, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Check that XV - X = V evaluates to 5 = 5.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick from '+' to numeral
matchstick.principle: Moving the vertical component of a '+' operator to a numeral simultaneously changes '+' to '-' and increases the numeral’s value by one (or decreases it if moved the opposite way).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a numeral can accept a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' to I turns '+' into '-' and I into II.

matchstick.title: Horizontal stick transfer between operators
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' (or vice versa) swaps the operators: '-' becomes '=', and '=' becomes '-', while both remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '=' and '-' and swapping them can balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Changing 'XV = X - V' to 'XV - X = V' by moving a horizontal from '=' to '-'.

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: V and X consist solely of diagonal sticks; removing one leaves a shape that does not correspond to any allowed numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never use V or X as the source of a stick; only move sticks from characters that contain vertical or horizontal components.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick may transform an operator into a shape that is not among the permitted symbols (+, -, =).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any move involving an operator, verify that the resulting symbol is still a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: The effect of moving a stick depends on the shape; a single stick typically changes a numeral by at most one unit (or two for I‑V reordering).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Use known value‑change rules (e.g., vertical stick = ±1, I‑V reordering = ±2) and avoid assuming larger jumps.

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver may think the move works without verifying the numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the values of both sides after the move and confirm the equality before answering.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: Diagonal sticks belong to V and X and cannot be used as vertical sticks; they have a different orientation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Keep track of stick orientation; only move vertical sticks to vertical positions and horizontal sticks to horizontal positions.
